data.title: Annual Report
features: Page numbers, headers and footers on every page (@page margin boxes)
CSS grid, flexbox, tables with colspan, multi-column text, counters
Inline SVG charts: bars, a line, and a donut
Vector QR code and Code 128 barcode on the cover
A 150-row ledger that flows across pages
Partials, macros, loops, conditions and filters
Filipino, Cyrillic, Greek and Vietnamese text in one font
Transforms, opacity, CSS variables and calc()
data.quote: We make a document in the time it takes to blink, on the customer's own device.
paragraphs: The year began with cautious optimism and ended with record volumes. Demand from the regions grew faster than we planned for, and our teams adapted by moving work closer to customers and simplifying how documents are produced.

Revenue rose steadily through the second half. The largest gains came from repeat customers, while new accounts took longer to convert than in previous years, a pattern we expect to ease as onboarding improves.

Costs grew more slowly than revenue. Savings in document handling, printing and shipping offset higher wages, and the move to generating documents on the customer's own device removed a whole class of server work.

Looking ahead we will keep investing in speed and reliability. Every report in this pack, including this one, is produced in a few milliseconds, which lets us send documents the moment a customer asks for them.
Risks remain: supplier prices, currency movements and the pace of regional expansion. We hold reserves for each and review them every quarter with the board.
We thank our customers, partners and every member of the team for a year of steady, careful work.

images-base64.label: Images: base64 (data: URI)
images-base64.template:
An image inside the template

The picture below is a PNG written as text in the data (a data: URI). It needs no network and no file, so it works everywhere.

You can also write it straight into the HTML: <img src="data:image/png;base64,iVBOR...">.

PNG, JPEG and GIF work. Tip: keep the picture small, because it travels inside the data.

images-url.label: Images: from a URL
images-url.template:
An image from a web address

The browser downloads it when the PDF is made, so the host must allow it (CORS). GitHub's raw file host does.

The address is a value in the data, so you can change it in the Data tab.

If the image is missing, the PDF is still made: a broken image is skipped, never an error.

images-mapped.label: Images: by name (your logo)
images-mapped.template:
Your logo here

This page asked for <img src="logo">. The name logo is a file, Blob or bytes you pass in images: { logo }. Use the Logo button at the top to choose your own picture (PNG, JPEG or GIF) and watch it change.

Passing images by name keeps big pictures out of the template and out of the data.

images-svg.label: Images: inline SVG (vector)
images-svg.template:
Vector drawings

An <svg> element written in the template is drawn as shapes: sharp at any zoom, and the file stays small.

Note: an <img> that points at an .svg file is not drawn yet. Paste the <svg> into the template, or use PNG.
